# 26.451: The table family, in the two backends that declined it

Status: recorded
Date: 2026-09-20
Source: `project.md` section 26, where it was written

**Twenty-five of situ's forty-two standard kernels were generated by C and
by neither Rust nor Python.** Measured by asking each backend's
`_for_kernel` for every codec in `std/kernels.situ`, which is the question
the emitters themselves answer: C handles seven families and the other two
handled POLYNOMIAL and ONES_COMPLEMENT.

This builds TABLE in both, which covers five of the twenty-five --
`base16`, `base16_lower`, `code_4b5b`, `manchester_802_3` and
`manchester_thomas`. The PADDED table codes are not among them: `base32`
and `base64` emit whole groups and fill a partial one, so the last group's
symbol count depends on how much input was left, which symbol-at-a-time
cannot express. C keeps that in a function of its own and so will this.

**The derivation is imported, not copied.** `_symbol_map` and
`NAMED_CODES` come from `c/derived.py`, which is what 0017's amendment
prescribes -- "a second backend re-spells; it does not re-derive" -- and
it means there is still exactly one copy of the 4b5b table in the tree.
Only the spelling is new, plus MSB-first bit helpers each backend needs
and C takes from its runtime.

**Checked against the standards, because C is not an oracle here.** C was
the only backend generating these, so a diff against its output would be
asking the implementation whether it agrees with itself -- the
one-witness-twice failure. What the tests assert instead is what the
standards say: `0xAB 0xCD` encodes to `ABCD` (RFC 4648), nibbles 0 and 1
to `11110 01001` (ANSI X3.263), and bits 0 and 1 to `01 10` for IEEE
802.3 and `10 01` for G.E. Thomas's, which is the bit-inverse and a
different code. Both backends were run, not read: Rust through `rustc`
and Python by executing the generated module.

**The undefined-symbol control is the half a round trip cannot show.** A
decoder that accepted everything would round-trip perfectly, so each case
also feeds bytes no codeword in that table defines and requires 0.

**The helper was unconditional at first, and the corpus said so.** Emitting
the bit helpers in every module changed **84 generated files** -- every
Rust and Python derived module in the corpus gaining thirty lines nothing
in them calls. Conditioned on a TABLE codec actually being bound, the
count is **2**, both of them `std/kernels.situ`'s. A generated file that
grows for a feature its schema does not use is a diff its reader has to
explain.

**And the first corpus diff measured the wrong thing.** It compared
`situc build` output, which does not emit derived bodies at all -- the
change lives in `gen-derived`. The empty result was real and answered a
question nothing had asked, which is this file's oldest lesson arriving in
a new place: ask the object you mean.
